findings.title: Enforce the shared domain/instance identity invariant in result admission
findings.counterexample: Construct two valid result edges with identical domain and instance strings, different consumers, and configuration values config-a/config-b (or different package identity). Give each a Resolved outcome with representative 0/1 and empty active_features/selected/needs/conflicting_edges/defaults_used. admit_request accepts the edges because duplicate detection compares full ConfigurationInstance. admit_result also compares full instance equality, so the two different configurations are treated as distinct instances and coverage succeeds. decode_result therefore accepts this result. The public resolver groups by domain+instance and correctly rejects the identical edge input as configuration/package disagreement.
findings.meaning: The new public result codec admits a result that violates the exact instance identity law and cannot be produced by its own resolver. This is semantic admission of known identity data, not a request to re-run definition solving inside the codec. It undermines the generated request/result owner/domain/provenance contract and the permanent M05B2-CONSUMERS rule that a reused instance cannot change package/configuration.
findings.correction: Share or apply the same domain+instance consistency check at wire admission so incompatible configuration/package identities refuse before any result is admitted. Add one focused codec regression with conflicting same-key edges and keep the existing different-domain positive. No new engine, full suite or extra platform gate required.
findings.evidence_kind: Deterministic source-derived counterexample; reviewer ran no Rust test or reproduction.
